Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2219; unleavened, i.e. (figuratively) uncorrupted; (in the neutral plural) specially (by implication) the Passover week:--unleavened (bread).
BiblicalUsage: Unleavened means without leaven — the bread of the Passover, eaten in haste the night of the exodus, and the feast kept for seven days after. The disciples asked where to prepare the Passover, the chief priests plotted to take Jesus during the feast, and Paul says to purge out the old leaven, for even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe unleavened bread is the picture of a life without the old leaven of malice and wickedness. I hold that Christ, our passover, was sacrificed so I could keep the feast in sincerity and truth.
